title: 40 KB Photo Size: Compress Photo to 40 KB | SahiSize
description: Get the 40 KB photo size DSSSB uses for thumb impressions: a 36–40 KB JPG of any photo or print. Free, made on your phone, never uploaded.
h1: 40 KB photo size: compress photo to 40 KB
intro: Get the 40 KB photo size DSSSB uses for thumb impressions. Add your image and download a JPG of 36–40 KB, made on your own phone with nothing uploaded.

steps.name: Add your image
steps.text: Take a photo or pick one from your gallery. JPG, PNG, WebP and iPhone HEIC files all work.

steps.name: Check the target
steps.text: 40 KB is already selected. Type a minimum if your form sets one, and decide whether the pixel size may change.

steps.name: Let it work
steps.text: The tool tries the highest JPEG quality that stays under 40 KB and makes the picture smaller only when it has to.

steps.name: Download
steps.text: When every line of the pass check has a tick, save the JPG and upload it to your form.

faq.q: Do the left and right thumb need the same size?
faq.a: For DSSSB both have the same 40 KB cap. Compress each image on this page and you get two files of 36–40 KB.

faq.q: Can I photo resize to 40 KB and keep the exact pixels?
faq.a: Yes, switch on Keep dimensions. The width and height stay the same and only the JPEG quality changes.

faq.q: Is 40 KB too large for a 30–49 KB rule?
faq.a: No. A file of 36–40 KB sits inside 30–49 KB with about nine kilobytes to spare under the cap.
No. Compression runs inside your browser on your own device. The page even works offline after your first visit.

sections.h2: Where you need to compress a photo to 40 KB
paras: DSSSB (Delhi) asks for both the left and the right thumb impression as images of up to 40 KB. The same target fits the RRB NTPC, ALP and Group D signature, which must be 30–49 KB, and the 20–50 KB photo and thumb rules on IBPS, SBI and RBI forms.

sections.h2: Quality when you convert a photo into a 40 KB JPG
paras: Forty kilobytes gives a fingerprint or a passport photo plenty of room. Ridges, pores and hairlines stay distinct, and the JPG shows no blocking at normal zoom.

As a rough guide, a passport-style photo on a plain background stays clean at about 240×320 pixels in 40 KB. A busy background or a dim, noisy shot needs more kilobytes for the same size, and a signature on white paper needs far fewer.

Whatever you add, the download is a baseline JPG (not progressive) between 36 and 40 KB. It stays under 40,000 bytes, so it passes whether the portal counts 1 KB as 1000 or 1024 bytes, and hidden camera and location data are removed.
Make the two DSSSB thumb impressions separately: crop each print to a square around the ridges, then compress. Do not put both thumbs in one image unless the form asks for it.
Pick the size just under the limit printed on your form. If the form gives both a minimum and a maximum, a range page fills in the minimum for you.
